exposureAnalysis: Sub-dependency of Next.js 15 SSR compiler. In LocalSampark, CSS parsing occurs at build time via Next.js Webpack/Turbopack; no user-supplied CSS strings are compiled at runtime.
mitigation: Requires upgrade to Next.js 16 (breaking framework upgrade with major router changes). Planned for post-launch milestone.
resolved: 2026-11-10 (F-135): fixed without a Next.js upgrade. Root package.json overrides next -> postcss ^8.5.32; npm audit reports no postcss advisory.

description: node-fetch denial of service / header leakage
exposureAnalysis: Sub-dependency of TensorFlow.js face-api model used strictly within isolated face verification worker; does not handle arbitrary outbound URLs.
mitigation: Upstream face-api.js maintainers have not released a v3 update. Replacing face-api requires vendor model migration.
resolved: 2026-11-10 (F-135): fixed. Root package.json overrides @tensorflow/tfjs-core -> node-fetch ^2.7.0 (same major API; face-api.js loads models from disk and never fetches).

scope: apps/mobile: expo-router@6 -> query-string@7.1.3 -> decode-uri-component@0.2.x (npm audit reports decode-uri-component, query-string and expo-router as three high entries)
description: decode-uri-component <=0.5.0: exponential/quadratic-time decoding of malformed percent-encoded input (DoS)
exposureAnalysis: The vulnerable function is only reached through query-string parse()/decode(). expo-router 6 calls only queryString.stringify (build/fork/getPathFromState*.js); its one parse() call is commented out (getStateFromPath.js:538). The app code imports neither package (grep app/ src/). Worst case if reached: a crafted deep link hangs the JS thread on the device that opened it; no data exposure and no server impact.
mitigation: No CommonJS release of query-string or decode-uri-component contains the fix (both moved to ESM-only), so an override would break expo-router at runtime. The fix is Expo SDK 58 (expo-router 58.0.30+), a major framework upgrade. Re-check at every Expo upgrade.

exposureAnalysis: Development and build-time CLI toolchain dependency for local Expo metro bundler SSL certificates. Never packaged into release APK or runtime bundle.
resolved: 2026-11-10 (F-135): fixed. npm audit fix moved apps/mobile node-forge to a patched release within range.

description: Check dependencies for packages that should not be installed directly

mitigation: Review dependency tree in Phase V6.
resolved: 2026-11-10 (F-134): fixed. @expo/config-plugins removed from apps/mobile dependencies (still provided by expo); expo-doctor passes this check.

description: Check for app config fields that may not be synced in a non-CNG project
exposureAnalysis: Native Android project uses prebuild / bare workflow (`apps/mobile/android`), where some fields in `app.json` are synced manually to native gradle files.
resolved: 2026-11-10 (F-134): replaced. The doctor check is switched off in apps/mobile/package.json and replaced by __tests__/nativeConfigSync.test.js, which compares the committed android/ project with `expo config --type introspect`. G9 fails unless that suite passes in the same run (scripts/verify/doctor-checks.mjs).

scope: apps/mobile: expo -> @expo/metro -> metro@0.83 -> image-size@1.2.1 (build tool only)
description: image-size 0.6.3-2.0.2: infinite loop (DoS) in the JXL/HEIF/ICNS parsers
exposureAnalysis: Used only by the Metro bundler at build time, to read the dimensions of the image files in this repository. It is not in the APK and never sees user-supplied images. Worst case: a crafted image committed to the repo hangs a build.
mitigation: No 1.x release is fixed. 2.x changed the API Metro calls (default export of a path -> named imageSize(buffer)), so an override breaks bundling. Fixed by the Metro release in a later Expo SDK.
